hero.subtitle: A practical guide to reading the archive, finding adaptations and extras, using the built-in readers, understanding the stats, and reporting problems.

categories.title: New Fan Guide
categories.description: What to consume first, and why

sections.title: New fan guide: what should I consume first?

items.question: The short answer: start with the light novels.
items.answer: The light novels are the source material for Adachi to Shimamura. If you want the fullest version of the story and the best place to understand the characters, start with Volume 1 and read the novels in publication order.

items.question: 1. Light novels — the main source material
items.answer: Start with Light Novels → Volume 1, then continue through the numbered volumes in order. The novels are the foundation of the story, so this is the recommended route if you are completely new or want the most complete experience.

items.question: 2. Manga — adaptations and alternate presentations
items.answer: The manga are adaptations of the story, not the primary source. They are great if you prefer visual storytelling, want to revisit familiar scenes, or want to see how the manga versions interpret the characters and moments.

items.question: 3. Anime — a visual adaptation
items.answer: The anime is another adaptation of the light novels. It is an easy entry point if you discovered Adachi and Shimamura through animation, but it does not replace the novels. If you start with the anime and want the fuller story afterward, going back to Light Novels → Volume 1 is the safest way to experience everything from the beginning.

items.question: 4. Extra stories and special novels
items.answer: Once you are familiar with the main story, explore Extra Stories and the special novel material. These are best treated as supplemental reading rather than your starting point. When an extra is clearly tied to a particular volume or release, reading the corresponding main material first can help avoid spoilers or missing context.

items.question: 5. Drama CDs, music, gallery, and other material
items.answer: These are complementary parts of the archive. Enjoy Drama CDs and Music when you want more audio material, and browse the Gallery, Timeline, and Constellation sections when you want references, visual material, or ways to explore the series outside the main narrative.

items.question: Already watched the anime?
items.answer:
If you are coming from the anime, you can continue the story from approximately chapter 26 of the manga, which corresponds to the point right after volume 4 of the light novel. If you prefer to continue directly with the light novels, you can start with volume 5.

However, if you want to enjoy the story with greater depth and experience the original narrative, we recommend reading the light novels from volume 1. This way, you can discover the monologues, the characters' inner thoughts, and scene details that were omitted in the adaptations.

items.question: What is AdaShimaverse?
items.answer: AdaShimaverse is an unofficial, non-profit fan archive for Adachi to Shimamura. It brings together reference material and fan-accessible resources for the series in one place.

items.question: What can I find here?
items.answer: The menu currently includes Anime, Manga, Novels, Extra Stories, Drama CD, Music, Gallery, Timeline, Constellation, Stats, Others, and About. Each section is built for a different kind of material, so you do not have to search the entire site to find what you want.

items.question: Where should I start reading?
items.answer: If you want the main story, open Novels. For manga material, use Manga. Extra Stories contains shorter side material and includes its own bookmarks and reading-progress features.

items.question: Is the material official?
items.answer: No. AdaShimaverse is a fan-made archive and is not an official website of the creators, publisher, or rights holders. The site itself is non-profit. Use the About section for project information, credits, and links to the original work.

items.question: Can I use AdaShimaverse on my phone?
items.answer: Yes. The site is designed to work on smaller screens. On mobile, use the floating menu button to open navigation and settings. If you prefer not to see that button on other pages, it can be disabled in the menu settings.

items.question: How do I read a novel or manga volume?
items.answer: Open Novels or Manga, choose a volume, and select Read. The document opens in the site's reader instead of taking you to a separate page.

items.question: What can I do in the PDF reader?
items.answer: The reader supports zoom in/out, zoom reset, previous/next page, direct page navigation, fullscreen, thumbnails, and cascade mode for continuous scrolling. The available controls can vary slightly between readers.

items.question: What is Cascade mode?
items.answer: Cascade mode displays the document as a continuous vertical stream instead of one page at a time. It is useful when you want to scroll naturally through a long document. Switching back to the normal mode returns to single-page navigation.

items.question: Can I download a book?
items.answer: Where a download is provided, the reader exposes the available formats through its download controls. The novel archive can provide PDF and EPUB files; availability depends on the individual volume.

items.question: What are the reader keyboard shortcuts?
items.answer: In the novel and manga PDF readers, Left Arrow moves to the previous page, Right Arrow moves to the next page, 0 resets zoom, and F toggles fullscreen. The PDF reader also recognizes Page Up/Page Down; avoid using shortcuts while typing in a page or search field.

items.question: How do bookmarks and reading progress work?
items.answer: Extra Stories can save bookmarks and reading progress in your browser. Progress is tracked as you read, and bookmarked stories can be filtered from the library. These are local browser features, not an account-based sync system.

items.question: What happens if I clear my browser data?
items.answer: Some site preferences and local reading data are stored in your browser. Clearing the site's local storage or browsing data can remove things such as Extra Stories bookmarks, reading progress, reader preferences, or language/settings saved locally.

items.question: What does each main section contain?
items.answer: Novels and Manga focus on volumes and chapters; Extra Stories collects shorter side material; Anime covers the animated adaptation; Drama CD and Music focus on audio material; Gallery is for visual material; Timeline organizes events; Constellation is a reference/exploration feature; Stats provides site data; and Others collects miscellaneous material.

items.question: How do I find a specific title?
items.answer: Use the search box when a section provides one. In the library pages, search can narrow entries by information such as title, description, or volume. If a search gives no result, try a shorter part of the title or another spelling.

items.question: Can I switch between Grid and List views?
items.answer: Some library pages provide Grid and List views. Use the view controls near the top of the library when they are available.

items.question: Where are the original-work links?
items.answer: The menu includes an Support the Original Work area with links to the official light novel, manga, and the author's web novel/blog resources. These links are external and open outside AdaShimaverse.

items.question: What are Timeline and Constellation for?
items.answer: Timeline is for chronological reference, while Constellation is an interactive reference feature for exploring relationships and details across the series. They are useful when you want context rather than simply reading a volume.

items.question: Which interface languages are available?
items.answer: The site's interface includes English, Spanish, and Tagalog in the main site localization. Individual sections or pieces of content may have different language availability depending on the material.

items.question: How do I change the language?
items.answer: Open the menu, find the Language setting, and choose the language you want. The selection is saved locally in your browser so it can be restored on a later visit.

items.question: What is Time-based appearance?
items.answer: Time-based appearance automatically changes the site's appearance according to the time of day. You can turn this behavior off and use the available appearance options from the menu instead.

items.question: What does the Mobile menu button setting do?
items.answer: It controls whether the floating mobile menu button is shown on other pages. The homepage keeps its menu button available regardless of this setting.

items.question: Do I need an account?
items.answer: No account is required for the site's normal browsing and reading features. Some preferences are kept locally in your browser rather than tied to a user account.

items.question: What is the difference between Novels, Manga, and Extra Stories?
items.answer: Novels is the main light-novel archive. Manga covers the manga adaptations and their volumes. Extra Stories is for shorter or supplemental material that is easier to browse as individual stories. Treat the sections as separate collections rather than three versions of the same library.

items.question: Why do some entries have labels such as Special, Short Story, or Upcoming?
items.answer: Those labels describe how an entry is classified in the archive. Special marks material such as Volume 99.9, Short Story marks the short-story collections, and Upcoming is used for a volume that has a known release but is not yet part of the released archive.

items.question: Why can page counts differ from the printed book?
items.answer: The archive's page count is based on the pages represented by the stored document and its recorded page range. Front matter, numbering conventions, scans, or other document differences can make an archive count differ from a publisher's advertised page count. Use the recorded page range when you need to understand exactly what the archive is counting.

items.question: How should I read material tied to a particular volume?
items.answer: When an extra story, illustration, or other item clearly belongs to a specific release, reading the corresponding main volume first is the safest approach. This preserves context and reduces the chance of encountering a character, event, or reference before its intended point in the series.

items.question: Why is some content available in one language but not another?
items.answer: The interface and the archive's source material are separate things. The site interface supports multiple languages, but an individual book, article, gallery entry, or other resource may only have a source or translation in certain languages. Missing language options do not necessarily mean the underlying item is missing.

items.question: Where can I check the source or official release information?
items.answer: Use the relevant item page, the Timeline, Gallery metadata, or the About section depending on what you are checking. When the archive provides an external official-work link, prefer that source for publisher or creator information rather than treating the fan archive as the authority.

items.question: What do the main totals count?
items.answer: The Statistics page separates the tracked collection from released material. Chapter and page totals exclude upcoming entries that do not have recorded page counts, while the tracked-volume count can include an upcoming release.

items.question: How is translation delay calculated?
items.answer: Translation delay is the number of days between the recorded Japanese release date and the recorded English completion date. It is an archive metric, not a measure of how long an official publisher took to publish an English edition.

items.question: What does the publication gap measure?
items.answer: A publication gap is the number of days between the Japanese release dates of consecutive released entries included in the statistics. It describes the spacing of releases, not the time required to write or translate a volume.

items.question: Why does an upcoming volume appear in some statistics but not others?
items.answer: Upcoming material is useful when describing the collection as a whole, so it can appear in tracked-volume or category counts. It is excluded from metrics that require completed page counts, chapters represented in the released archive, or a completed translation date.

items.question: Can the statistics change?
items.answer: Yes. The page is generated from the archive's statistics data, so corrections to dates, page counts, classifications, or release status can change the results. The numbers should be read as a snapshot of the archive's current dataset rather than immutable facts.

items.question: What is the best way to use the Charts section?
items.answer: Use the charts for comparisons rather than absolute conclusions. Pages per Volume and Chapters per Volume compare structure; Cumulative Pages shows the running size of the released collection; and Translation Delay shows how the recorded JP-to-EN interval varies between entries.

items.question: A page is completely blank. What should I do?
items.answer: First, reload the page. If it remains blank, try a hard refresh, then try opening the page in a private/incognito window or another browser. If only one page is affected, include that exact page in your bug report.

items.question: The reader opens but the document is blank or stuck loading.
items.answer: Give the document a moment to load, then refresh the page. Check that JavaScript is enabled and that your browser or content-blocking extension is not blocking the document resources. If another browser works, report the original browser and the affected volume.

items.question: Images, audio, or a specific item is missing.
items.answer: Reload the page and check your connection first. If the rest of the site works but one item does not, the problem may be specific to that asset. Report the exact title, volume, track, or gallery item so it can be investigated.

items.question: The site looks outdated after an update.
items.answer: Your browser may still have an older cached asset. Try a hard refresh. If you installed the site or use offline caching, close and reopen it so the latest assets can be loaded.

items.question: My bookmarks or reading progress disappeared.
items.answer: Extra Stories bookmarks and reading progress are stored locally in your browser. They can disappear if site data was cleared, local storage was reset, or you changed to a different browser/device. There is currently no account-based sync for these local features.

items.question: A download says the file is unavailable.
items.answer: The file may not currently be available for that item. Try again later and check whether another format is offered. If a file that used to work has stopped working, include the exact volume or item when reporting it.

sections.title: Report a problem or suggest an improvement

items.question: What should I report?
items.answer: You can report broken pages, missing files, incorrect information, translation mistakes, broken links, reader problems, visual bugs, or anything else that is preventing you from using the site normally.

items.question: What information makes a bug report useful?
items.answer: Include the page or section, title/volume/chapter, browser and device when relevant, and a short description of what you expected versus what happened. A screenshot or console error can also help when the problem is visual or technical.

items.question: Can I suggest a feature?
items.answer: Yes. Suggestions for new features, navigation improvements, reader controls, archive organization, or quality-of-life changes are welcome. Explain the problem the feature would solve rather than only describing the button you want added.

items.question: Where do I send feedback?
items.answer: Use the site's Send Feedback form when it is available. For project information, credits, and other official site details, see the About section.

items.question: Who owns the original series?
items.answer: Adachi and Shimamura and its original characters, artwork, and related works belong to their respective rights holders. AdaShimaverse is an unofficial fan project and does not claim ownership of the original work.
